quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. rationale: Section 21 meets the preferred position. The cap is expressly mutual and set at the greater of 12 months' Fees "paid or payable" and USD 1,000,000 (§21.1); "Fees" (§1.5) is a substantive base covering subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the cap is not illusory. §21.2 is a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and helpfully confirms data-restoration, replacement-service, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages. §21.3 places outside the cap breaches of confidentiality, data-protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP, and confirms Customer's payment of undisputed Fees is not "damages" subject to the cap. §21.4 preserves liability that cannot lawfully be limited, and §18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. No one-sided or hidden liability limitation appears elsewhere in the document. No redline needed.

quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
rationale: Section 7.2 (the first clause numbered 7.2) conditions our ability to engage any other provider on first disclosing a competing offer and giving Vendor the chance to match it. It also directly conflicts with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment. The exclusivity that runs in our favour (e.g. Section 12.3) is untouched. The price-matching/MFN aspect is separately relevant under the MFN rule; here the deletion is driven by the restraint on our sourcing freedom.

Section 7.2 imposes an MFN/right-to-match obligation on us, the Customer: before engaging another provider we must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer we receive. It is unlimited as to product, term, and comparison methodology, so it falls short of the fallback (defined product, 12 months, reasonable-comparison carve-outs) and sits in walk-away territory as an open-ended obligation to extend Vendor any better third-party terms. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment. No Vendor-granted MFN exists elsewhere to preserve, and there is no separate exclusivity covenant, so this is flagged once here under MFN as the primary breach.</parationale>

The 30-day return clock now runs from expiry or termination rather than from a request, and the format is a standard machine-readable format, matching our standard position of up to six months' assistance at your then-current rates and certified deletion after return.

ops.text: 10.3 Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of expiry or termination, return all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

quote: On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.
rationale: Section 10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination) covers only loss of access, Deliverable delivery and refunds. It references "any agreed transition period" but creates no obligation on Vendor to provide transition assistance, and nothing anywhere in the Agreement requires return or export of Customer Data in a usable format or certified deletion. Section 16.5 expressly carves Customer Data out of the return/destroy duty and defers to "Sections 11 and 15" — Section 11 does not exist in the document, and Section 15 addresses processing and privacy only, not exit. The Agreement therefore fails even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days), leaving our data with no guaranteed retrieval path. Inserted a new Section 10.3 at the preferred position: up to six months' transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, return in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter (subject to routine backup/legal retention, consistent with Section 16.5).
